Job Summary I&E Technician performs various duties related to the maintenance, troubleshooting, installation, and repair of all instrumentation, control systems, and electrical equipment associated with a combined cycle power generation facility. This position is in a bargaining unit represented by the Utility Workers of America/AFL-CIO and Local 310 BUW Council UWUA, AFL-CIO. Major Pieces of Equipment to include, but not limited to: Combustion Turbines Steam Turbines Heat Recovery Steam Generators 50 MW and 120 MW Generators Surface Condensers Circulating Water Equipment Station And Instrument Air Systems Distributed Controls Systems Auxiliary components to include, but not limited to: Demineralizer Equipment Ammonia Injection Equipment Closed Cooling Water System Equipment Fuel Oil/Gas Equipment Air Removal Equipment Hydrogen Seal Oil Equipment Feedwater/Condensate Equipment Steam Dump Equipment Turbine Bypass Equipment Waste Water Treatment Equipment SCR Equipment CEMs (Continuous Emission Monitoring Equipment) Turbine Supervisory Instrumentation Plant Electrical Systems Programmable Logic Controllers Assist and advise Management and Plant Operators on all instrumentation and electrical equipment and systems. Perform scheduled preventive and predictive maintenance activities, to include, but not limited to: Readings Inspections and Checks Lubrication Equipment Cleanings Filter Changes Analyze equipment performance by processing test data, using schematic drawings, diagrams and reviewing equipment manuals. Recommend and/or take necessary corrective action. Maintain, repair, and troubleshoot all control systems at station. Which include, but are not limited to: Honeywell Experion Siemens T3000 Honeywell TDC3000 Allen Bradley Use hand tools, power tools, test and calibration equipment to perform maintenance activities. Maintain and update shop records including prints, drawings, and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) manuals. Use computer to retrieve job-related data. Handle and/or dispose of hazardous materials and waste products to include cleaning of spills. Participate in on-the-job training, initially as a trainee in the progression program, then as an OJT trainer for other personnel. Maintain, clean, and properly store shop equipment and tools. Comply with all company safety and compliance (environmental and NERC) regulations, including safe work practices as described in the company Safety Policies, Station Safety Procedures, and use of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE). Perform work assignments within other departments at times of peak loads, major operating problems, emergency situations. Conduct lock out tag out (LOTO) activities within system and plant rules and regulations. undefined Perform Work Authorization Paperwork as directed by Management and Company Procedures. undefined Participate and Contributes to Plant Safety Meetings and Programs. Brings ideas for Safety improvements forward. Documents all safety findings appropriately (near miss reporting, safety work orders, incident investigation participation, and safety improvement plans). Stops work and takes corrective action if an unsafe act is witnessed and escalates to management as appropriate. Enforces site safety rules and practices. undefined Participates in the upkeep of the facility (i.e. snow removal, walkway salting, etc.) undefined Research, procure, and order parts and materials, as required. undefined Maintains good housekeeping. The hourly rate for this position is governed by the Collective Bargaining Agreement. The hourly rate for this position is $48.62 This position requires the ability to work 8 consecutive hours of work on a standard daily shift, with the potential for both emergent (call-in) and planned support. The company values work/life balance, however, a requirement of this job that emergent overtime will be worked occasionally, and planned overtime will be worked during high peak times. Education and Experience – An equivalent combination of education, training and experience will be considered. High School Diploma (or equivalent) Two years of trade or technical school with training in the fundamentals of The Power Plant Cycle preferred. Six years experience in maintenance, repair and troubleshooting of instrument and electrical (I&E) systems, and equipment in a power plant or similar industrial setting. Demonstrated ability in reading process & instrumentation diagrams, electrical one-line diagrams and logic diagrams, and use of test equipment through a practical exam Complete accredited courses in (or possess a certificate of equivalent training earning CEUs): Basic College Math/Algebra Basic Electricity Basic Electronics Complete the Hiring Process (including background check and drug screening). Complete the Progression Program within required intervals. Obtain RI Crane Operators license. Experience with High Voltage Test Equipment. Obtain a RI Journeyman Electrician license within 5 years. Obtain ISA Level I Certified Control System Specialist certification within 5 years. Valid driver’s license. All communication concerning the testing is sent to the candidate's email address provided during the application process. **Level of position will be determined by applicable skills/experience. Ability in the following areas; basic math, electricity, chemistry and power plant physical sciences; print reading; communication skills. Competency is demonstrated through satisfactory completion of accredited courses. Company courses or equivalency exams Ability to perform technical troubleshooting. Ability to communicate effectively orally using telephone and PA system. Ability to use a computer effectively, including: Word, Excel, PI, time keeping , computer based training, and other needs as technology changes over time. Ability to work on and troubleshoot on Server Based Control Systems. Ability to read and interpret blue prints, drawings, panel schedules, etc. Work Environment – Environmental or atmospheric conditions commonly associated with the performance of the functions of this job. Work on ladders and scaffolding, work at heights, work in high noise and/or temperature extreme environments, work near high voltage and/or rapidly rotating equipment and work in cramped and/or confined positions with occasional heavy lifting. Be able to operate fork lifts, manlifts, and overhead cranes in performance of job. Work is often physical and in atmospheric conditions where fumes, dust, and gases are present. Work overtime (e.g., scheduled, unscheduled, and call-ins); be reachable by telephone and be willing to respond to around-the-clock plant problems. Occasional work with toxic chemicals including but not limited to solvents, acids, and caustics. PPE will be provided by the Company. Cost & Incentive Optimization:
Design and implement competitive, cost-effective temp worker incentive structures. Drive intelligent rostering strategies to achieve low, optimized Cost Per Hour (CPH).
Talent Pool Development:
Strategy-build and maintain a reliable pool of tenured/senior temporary workers to ensure shift stability, high quality, and fast operational ramp-ups.
Stakeholder & Agency Management:
Serve as the trusted partner to HUB Operations leaders. Collaborate daily with FC Manpower teams (given shared facility roofs), in-house talent acquisition, and external vendors/agencies.
Operations Analytics & Dashboarding:
Build scalable dashboards, data models, and tracking tables to showcase critical input metrics, labor show-up trends, and quality guardrails for leadership decision-making.

Experience:
4+ years of hands-on experience in workforce planning, labor modeling, or capacity planning within high-volume logistics, fulfillment centers or similar HVH operations
Analytical & Data Skills:

There are close to a billion knowledge workers in the world, and only a small fraction of them have discovered what it feels like to work alongside AI that actually raises their game. You'll define the Marketing & growth strategy by segment for our core knowledge-work products, and coordinate the work streams that acquire and activate both users and accounts and drive their success. This role provides direction, coordination, and fuel across Demand Generation, Growth, Brand, Events, Campaigns, Field Marketing, and Success.
This is a GTM-oriented product marketer: deep in messaging and product truth, expressed through narrative content, campaigns, activation programs, and community. You'll build and run programs personally from day one, backed by many internal teams.
If you've owned an awareness-to-success marketing motions end to end for a product line, know how to turn product truth into content and campaigns that land with various segments and personas, and want to build the motion that gets millions of knowledge workers to change how they work, this role is for you.
Key responsibilities
Define the Marketing and growth strategy, segment by segment.
Build a marketing plan per priority segment or function, prioritizing where to lead first and what to deliberately not do yet.
Set the content direction for Claude for Knowledge Work.
Shape flagship narrative content based on the plan and campaign needs, building on the messaging and launch foundations owned by Core PMM.
Turn activation into a flywheel inside enterprise accounts.
Identify and activate champions, coordinate workshops and webinars, and run lifecycle programs for various personas inside top accounts, inspiring knowledge workers to raise their ambitions and deliver more impact with Claude.
Own the flagship acquisition and activation campaigns.
Define and run the "Hand off your tasks to Claude" integrated programs, choosing channels and activations that fit the audience.
Inform the digital, social, and field motions.
Shape the Knowledge Work digital, social, and influencer motion — ops, finance, legal, marketing, and productivity creators — and our social presence in this space.
Coordinate without owning.
Provide direction, coordination, and fuel across Demand Generation, Growth, Brand, Events, Campaigns, Field Marketing, and Success, so the growth motion moves as one program without duplicating any team's mandate.
Build and ship the work yourself.
Operate as an individual contributor in year one — write the plans, build the campaigns, and ship the content directly, with room to grow a team as the motion matures.
Report on what the motion is actually driving.
Track and share progress against awareness and preference, growth (WAUs and enterprise account depth), revenue contribution, and campaign efficiency.

Excel at cross-functional collaboration, with a track record of driving work through influence across Demand Generation, Growth, Brand, Events, Campaigns, Field Marketing, and Success, without direct authority over any of them
Possess strong storytelling and content instincts, with a track record of flagship narrative content such as executive series or customer story programs
